sourceInformation.source: Basketball, over-the-top arcade style (genre inspiration; an original game)
sourceInformation.plan: PLAN.md. The title was drawn this run with a real RNG (secrets.randbelow) from 50 candidates: ZONEFIRE. The plan's own title (BASKETBLAM) was replaced.
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade sports: 2-on-2 basketball in the over-the-top arcade style, with a four-stop story tour
sourceInformation.perspective: Side-on broadcast camera (custom orthographic view, pitch 30 degrees, panning with the ball), with an optional High (three-quarter) camera
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 (modified copy, changes marked in the engine); AI Hub session client 1.4.0 (unmodified); plain JavaScript; Canvas 2D; Web Audio; Node 24 and Playwright 1.63.0 for the tests; the pause menu is the engine's standard Shell, themed in the game's colours and freezes the match
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's HD style pushed to 90s arcade broadcast: five courts (neon Skybox, sunset Pier, dusk Scrapyard, night Caldera, arena Blam Dome), new courts, props, crowds and lighting
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's rigs posed by math. Every celebration, taunt and dunk is a keyframed body clip (about 20 celebration clips, the same set for taunts, and one clip per dunk) over both hands, the body's height, the rig's pose and a squash. A hand layer solves both arms by inverse kinematics; a procedural dribble is synced to the ball; keyed body clips for pass, steal and shove; dunk spins for the 360 and 720 and a front flip. Lean is driven by the clips through the rig's lean option (a small engine read, marked as ours).
sourceInformation.audio: All music, sound effects and voices written in code: 12 songs, 8 stings, about 90 sound effects, a crowd ambience, and gibberish formant voices with captions
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world session (HUB SHOWDOWN): host-authoritative snapshots, input messages, the hub's card, leave, time-up and end handling, a server copy, and a session overlay that does not pause
sourceInformation.testing: 80 headless tests via node:vm; 3 browser tests (Playwright); 4 AI Hub harness scenarios; all pass on the final build
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux (WSL2); browser for the tests: Chromium; the player's browser unknown
sourceInformation.usage: About 0.7M tokens by the session's budget counter; API cost in USD unknown; about one hour of session time

testingFeedback: About 15 issues, found by the tests, the browser run and the hub harness; four were game-breaking: a ball trapped on the rim's centre, a quarter that never ended, players stuck in their jump, and the page failing to start without a body for the canvas
Four game-breaking issues (a ball trapped on the rim centre, a quarter that never ended, players stuck in their jump, the page failing to start); the rest minor
The full CPU-vs-CPU matches to the final whistle, with the event counts: they exposed most of the bugs that unit checks missed
The hub harness as a black box: two scenarios stalled at first. The cause was in our test, which left auto=1 out of the plan's two variants; the harness then waits for a manual start
engineFeedback: The HD rigs and the look out of the box; E.TileMap with floorTex; game.advance for fixed steps in tests; E.Dialog; the input labels and glyph names

Yes: E.arc's apex is the rise over the higher end, not an absolute height (first guessed wrong); the canvas needs document.body, so the scripts must sit at the end of body (a crash until fixed); the hand joints had to be read from solvePose
The shot model and its decided outcomes, the ball physics against the arena, rims and glass, the CPU brains, the match flow and the netcode, the voices and the songs
The ball against the rims and the arena walls, and posing a rig's hand from a target (the pose internals were not documented)

Four changes, each marked /* ZONEFIRE: ... */: public audio buses (sfxBus, musicBus); basketball shorts on the HD legs; hair styles afro, flattop and mohawk; a Dialog voice that may be a function. Each was needed for the game's look or its voices
A public hook for a rig's hand targets (so a pose layer needs no solvePose wrapping), and a canvas that is created on demand instead of needing document.body at script time
promptFeedback: The milestones, the tables of numbers and the list of tests: a clear target to build and check against
The goal and STAGE.md name the folder and the file differently, and the title came from the plan's pick rather than a pick of this run
The scope in one session: eleven milestones, about 230 tests and a hub check
Split it into a playable core first and the polish after, and give the hub check its own budget

aiHub.name: ZONEFIRE
aiHub.tagline: No fouls. No mercy. All BLAM.
aiHub.description: Over-the-top 2-on-2 arcade basketball on five courts with dunks, shoves, Supernova and a story tour against the robot Blambots. Up to four players, on one screen or online.
aiHub.controls: Stick or WASD moves · Square or Space shoots · Cross or E passes · R2 or Shift turbo · Circle or Q shoves · Triangle or F lobs
